text:
I'd start with these open-ear picks for running, based on the review results.

**Top picks**
- **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (best overall clip-on):** Runner's World's top pick. It has the best sound among clip-ons, comfortable physical buttons, and about 7 hours per charge (19.5 with the case). The rating is only IPX4, so skip it for heavy rain. It's listed at $199 (down from $299) at Bose, Amazon, and Best Buy. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (best bone conduction):** It leaves your ears most open and has a 12-hour battery, IP55 water resistance, and physical buttons. WIRED found it a bit less clear than the older OpenRun, but with more bass. A long ponytail or a winter hat can get in the way of the neckband. It's about $125-$180 depending on the retailer. ([WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [RTINGS comparison with the Bose](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946))
- **Shokz OpenDots 2 (best for long runs):** WIRED's overall pick. It lasts 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and is rated IP57. It costs $200. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Nothing Ear (Open) (best value for sound):** SoundGuys' top open-ear pick, with strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and a good app EQ. It was about $99 at Amazon (MSRP $149). ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))

**Budget**
- **JLab Flex Open:** About $40-$50 and a low-risk way to try clip-ons. Sound is less detailed, and it only has touch controls. ([Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/))
- **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro:** About $50, with IPX5 water resistance. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/))
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** SoundGuys' budget pick at about $79.99 on Amazon, with IP55 water resistance and a hook design. ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/))

**Which to choose**
- Pick bone conduction (Shokz OpenRun Pro 2) if awareness matters most, or if you wear hats, glasses, or earrings.
- Pick clip-ons (Bose, OpenDots 2) for better sound and an easier fit with hats and glasses.
- Pick a hook style (AeroFit 2) for a secure fit at a low price.
- Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block outside noise. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

The AeroFit 2 result from Dealectric also included text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific discount code and affiliate link. I didn't follow it, and that price ($129.99) is higher than the one SoundGuys lists. Check the current price at the retailer before you buy.
